issue.title: usage: a custom provider's balance meters ("…%" in the balance path) ignore the Left/Used switch
issue.body:
The Left/Used switch flips every subscription window, but a custom provider's balance meter always shows
the used share, both its figure and its bar.

**Reproduction**

1. Add a custom provider whose balance endpoint reports a daily allowance as a percent used, e.g. a reply of
   ```json
   { "windows": [ { "name": "daily", "used": 8.9 } ] }
   ```
   with
   ```
   magpie provider set <id> balance=<url> "balance.path=Daily: windows.0.used / 100%"
   ```
2. The provider's card shows `Daily 8.9%` with a bar filled to 8.9%. That is right for **Used**.
3. Switch the quota display to **Left** (Usage page, or the tray panel's Used/Left button).
4. Subscription cards now read `… left`. The custom provider's card still reads `Daily 8.9%` with an 8.9% bar.

**Expected:** with Left on, the balance meter reads `91.1% left` and its bar fills to 91.1%, like every other
window.

**Where it happens**

- `internal/provider/balance.go` `balanceAmount` / `balanceShare`: the part's `text` (`"8.9%"`) is formatted in
  Go as the used share. `percent` carries the same number for the bar.
- `internal/gui/assets/app.js` `panelBalances` (tray panel, `if (p.percent != null) card.append(balanceMeter(p.percent))`)
  and `balanceRow` (Usage page, same call): neither checks `quotaLeft`. `balanceMeter` fills to `percent` as is.
- Subscription windows go through `quotaFill` / `quotaText`, which do `quotaLeft ? 100 - used : used` and label
  `{n} left` / `{n} used`.

**Suggested fix**

For a balance part that has `percent`, render it the way `quotaText`/`quotaFill` render a window: with Left on,
show `100 − percent` and label it `left`, and fill the bar to the same share. Keep the "nearly full" colour keyed
to the used share. A part without `percent` (money, counts) is unchanged. The switch is already stored in
Settings, so the tray panel, the Usage page and any alert text would follow it the same way.

comments.body:
I carried this fix into the user fork, based on @ggbdpq’s [original patch](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/commit/579942e679de66090299ba73f8c071a9f9bfb89c), with attribution retained and broader browser coverage.

- Fix: [skygunner/magpie@15759adb](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/15759adb4a09dcafd0b11980ddc0cbae385c65bf).
- Branch: [`fix/balance-quota-left`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/balance-quota-left).

Both balance renderers now show `91.1% left` and fill the meter to 91.1% for the reported 8.9% usage when Left is selected. Switching to Used restores the reported figure and fill. Warning colours remain tied to the used share, and money/count balances retain their reported values. This changes presentation only; the provider’s raw balance data and history are preserved.

Verification at this fix:

- The new regression fails with the original renderer, waiting for `91.1% left`, and passes with the fix.
- 40 browser cases pass: Chromium and WebKit; en, zh, zh-TW, ja, de; Usage at 900/1280 px and panel at 440/360 px; Left and Used. These also click the actual panel switch and check the redrawn figures, fills, warning colour and unchanged money balance.
- The six other directly related balance/quota browser files contribute 56 passing cases (96 passing cases together with the new regression).
- Native, Linux (`nogui`) and Windows vet and builds pass, as does the full `go test -tags nogui ./...` run. The core app budget was raised by 100 bytes, with the reason documented: this shared tray/Usage renderer is 57 bytes over the previous limit after reusing the existing `quotaText` formatter.

An exploratory seven-file browser run also found a separate intermittent failure in `panel-usage.test.cjs` (59 pass, 1 fail). I reproduced its shared-request-log interference on the old renderer with a deliberate late panel request and filed [#3311](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3311). That pre-existing test issue is not claimed fixed here, and the whole browser suite is not claimed green.

The browser tests use isolated API fixtures, not real provider accounts. Native tray startup, macOS/Windows runtime, and the entire browser suite were not checked for this patch. No upstream PR was opened.

Verified the fork commit on top of `63be4771` (Windows, Go 1.26.8) as far as this machine reaches: cherry-picked 15759adb, checked the renderer change line by line against my `579942e6`, and ran the Go-side budget gate. The browser regression itself I could not run — no Playwright or browsers installed here, and installing them is outside what I'll do to this checkout unasked.

**What was verified**

- The renderer change matches my patch: the four `p.text` → `balanceText(p)` call sites and the `balanceMeter` body (`quotaLeft ? 100 - used : used`, nearly-full colour keyed to the used share) are verbatim mine. Left still means the meter fills with the remaining share and the warning colour still follows usage — no behavior fork there.
- `balanceText` is the one rewrite: mine computed the complement by hand (`t("{n} left", ...)`), this one delegates to the existing `quotaText`. I checked `quotaText` field by field — same clamp, same `100 - used`, same integer/`toFixed(1)` rounding, same `{n} left`/`{n} used` wording; its `unlimited` and `quotaCount` branches can't fire on `{used: percent}`. Output-equivalent, and the reuse is the better shape.
- Attribution in the commit is present and exact: `Co-authored-by: ggbdpq <ggbdpq@gmail.com>`, with "Adapt ggbdpq/magpie 579942e679de66090299ba73f8c071a9f9bfb89c" in the message. Author: vincent.
- The expanded regression is real: same file grown 123 → 136 lines, five languages (en, zh, zh-TW, ja, de) where mine had two, two Usage/panel width pairs where mine had one, and a `/api/settings/quota-left` route so the test clicks the actual panel switch instead of seeding the setting.

**Drift and landing**: the fork's parent is 478 commits ahead of `63be4771`. Two conflicts on this base. `app.js` is a mis-alignment only (this base already has `balanceShown`; the resolution keeps the one-line comment and the merged body). `core_budget_test.go` is substantive: the commit raises `appScriptBudget` by 100 because on the fork's base app.js is ~85 KB larger and the new renderer pushed it 57 bytes over. On this base that raise is not needed — with the original `1_250_000` kept, `go test -tags nogui -run '^TestCoreScriptBudget$' ./internal/gui/` passes (`ok` 1.252s), so landing here keeps this base's budget values and drops the commit's two budget comment lines; the renderer code itself lands as written. The doc paragraph in `gui-shell.md` lands as written. On today's main (`e00fbdbb`, checked 2026-10-23) the commit's whole diff applies clean (`apply --3way --check`); landing there should still keep main's current `appScriptBudget` — the +100 raise is the fork base's need only.

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Budget gate with this base's values | `go test -tags nogui -run '^TestCoreScriptBudget$' ./internal/gui/` | ok 1.252s |
| Merged app.js parses | `node --check internal/gui/assets/app.js` | ok |
| Vet / gofmt | `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gui/`; `gofmt -l core_budget_test.go` | clean |

**Gaps**: the red/green evidence for the behavior itself is the report's and mine from the original patch (its regression waits 5s for "91.1% left" on the old renderer), both unverified on this machine — the ablation here would need Playwright, which this checkout doesn't have. `TestProxyCheckSaysAProxyPassedBy` in the full gui package is red on this machine at the base too (pre-existing, matches the report's note); I did not run the full package. WebKit and real balance endpoints remain unverified on both sides.

Thanks — the quotaText reuse is the right call, and the wider language/viewport coverage plus the real-switch click close the gaps my test left.

Verified with AI assistance (GLM-5.3-Flash via ZCode); I've read the diff and re-ran the checks above.

Landed in 63cccbb47, with your authorship, in **v0.1.2583**: a custom provider's balance percent now follows the Left/Used switch. Follow-up 434982e5a (mine): the patch put the core script 330 bytes over TestCoreScriptBudget. balanceMeter and balanceText are now shorter, so it fits without raising the budget.

Review: balance-quota-left runs in both engines and every language. balance-fix has 9 reds per engine, but they are the same on main, so they are filed separately as #4682 and #4683. At the pushed head 768228a4f, on the test Mac: the full suite `go test -tags nogui -count=1 -timeout 45m ./...` is ok in all 87 packages (gateway 852.6s), plus `go vet ./...`, Linux and Windows `go vet`, and the budget tests in internal/gui. Reporter: please say here if v0.1.2583 still shows it wrong.
Reopened: the commit's "Fixes" line closed this automatically. It stays open until the reporter confirms v0.1.2583.

issue.title: Routing treats a readable balance as "allowance not known": providers with balance but no usage windows (e.g. MiniMax Code) always show unknown

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
### What happened

The Routing page shows 「剩余额度未知」 ("remaining allowance not known yet") for providers whose usage API returns a **balance but no windows**, even though magpie successfully read the balance.

**Root cause (verified in source):** `internal/provider/routing.go:502`:

```go
for user, q := range readings {
    if q.Error != "" || len(q.Windows) == 0 {
        continue
    }
    all[user] = allowanceOf(q.Windows, time.Now())...
}
```

A reading with `Windows: []` but a non-empty `Balance` is skipped entirely, so the account is treated as unknown.

**Real-world example (MiniMax Code, from `~/.config/magpie/quotas.json`):**

```json
"minimax-code/minimax336627": {
  "quota": {
    "provider": "minimax-code",
    "plan": "Free",
    "user": "MiniMax336627",
    "windows": [],
    "balance": "1740.72 credits",
    "readAt": "2026-10-23T14:51:39.6466365+08:00"
  }
}
```

The balance **is** read (1,740.72 credits) and even displayed on the Usage/provider page, but the Routing page says 「剩余额度未知」 and the router weights the account as if nothing were known (it falls into the `learns` path).

### Suggested fix

When `len(q.Windows) == 0` but `q.Balance != ""`, still build an `Allowance` — either as an unwindowed meter keyed off the balance text (there is precedent: balance meters already render on the Usage page), or at minimum surface `Known: true` with the balance so routing doesn't treat a readable account as unknown.

Related but distinct: #2333 (expose holds via CLI/JSON), #3193 (custom provider balance meter switch). This issue is specifically about the `Windows == 0 → unknown` branch in the routing path.
